title: The Ethics of Disclosure
text:
Journalists who publish leaked documents often face an uncomfortable dilemma. On the one hand, the public has a legitimate interest in knowing what powerful institutions are hiding. On the other, the disclosure may expose private individuals who had no say in the matter. Editors must weigh these competing obligations before deciding what to print.

Many newsrooms have therefore adopted internal codes that require reporters to justify every decision publicly. Such codes do not eliminate disagreement, but they create a record of reasoning that the audience can scrutinise. In this sense, accountability is not only a duty of the powerful but also of the press itself.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what may the disclosure expose?
options: Private individuals who had no say

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do many newsrooms require reporters to do?
The writer suggests that internal codes are useful mainly because they:
options: Guarantee that no errors will occur
Create a record of reasoning that the audience can examine
Protect reporters from any legal action

questions.text: By stating that accountability is 'also of the press itself', the writer implies that:
options: Journalists should be exempt from criticism
The press must also answer for its own choices
Powerful institutions no longer need oversight

vocabulary.definition: a situation in which a difficult choice must be made between two unwelcome options
the act of making previously hidden information known
examine something very carefully and critically
the obligation to explain and justify one's actions

paragraph_translations: Dziennikarze publikujący przecieki dokumentów często stają przed niewygodnym dylematem. Z jednej strony społeczeństwo ma uzasadniony interes w poznawaniu tego, co potężne instytucje ukrywają. Z drugiej strony ujawnienie może narazić prywatne osoby, które nie miały wpływu na sprawę. Redaktorzy muszą rozważyć te sprzeczne obowiązki, zanim zdecydują, co wydrukować.

Wiele redakcji przyjęło więc wewnętrzne kodeksy, które wymagają od reporterów publicznego uzasadniania każdej decyzji. Takie kodeksy nie eliminują sporów, ale tworzą zapis rozumowania, który odbiorcy mogą badać. W tym sensie odpowiedzialność nie jest wyłącznie obowiązkiem możnych, lecz także samej prasy.
